She found it at dawn among the kelp and rolled it in her palms like a relic. Inside, curled tight, was a note in faded ink: 'To whoever finds this — your light saved us the night our boat broke. We never got to thank you. We named our daughter after this coast.' Maren read it three times, then looked up at the tower, its lamp burning pale against the morning. She had never known which ships she had saved, only the beam, the fog, the long solitary hours. Somehow the loneliness felt lighter now. She tucked the note into her logbook, and that night she lit the lamp with unusual care.", "w02": "凌晨四点，城市像一头疲惫的巨兽，缓缓吐出最后一口热气。街道空旷，路灯把清洁工的影子拉得很长。写字楼的灯稀稀落落，像不肯闭上的眼睛。远处传来第一班地铁的轰鸣。便利店的灯光温暖而孤独，守着城市最后一点烟火气。早点铺的蒸笼冒出白汽，油条在锅里翻滚。这一刻的城市卸下白日喧嚣，露出最真实的模样——疲惫、温柔，又充满希望。再过两小时，它将重新醒来。", "w03": "- Imagine standing in a long line and wanting to know your number: you ask the person in front of you, and they ask the person in front of them, and so on down the line.\n- Everyone does the same tiny job — 'ask the person ahead' — until you reach the very first person, who simply says 'I'm number 1!' without asking anyone at all.\n- The answers then travel back, each person adding one, until you finally learn your own number — that's recursion: a function that calls itself on a smaller piece of the problem until it hits a simple case it can answer directly."}
